quote: I'll keep it short for you. My job here at Ion is just to put together this design to see if it's a good fit for the home. Just have a couple of quick questions for you.
stewart_read: Efficient framing of the call's purpose right after intro, setting expectations for a short qualifying conversation. This is a clean, functional opening that sets up the rest of the script well.
coaching_implication: No change needed here — this is a good model of a concise purpose-statement opener the rep can keep using.

quote:
the mainly just the prices of the electric bill recently
as well as
it's just easy to provide for myself and not have to worry about things like that.
stewart_read: Customer names bill pain unprompted as the primary motivator. This is exactly the anchor coaching_philosophy.bill_anchoring calls for, but the rep never returns to it — the call derails into the address-lookup problem and the bill amount is never asked.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to write down 'bill pain' the moment it's said and explicitly return to it once the address issue is resolved (or park the address and get the bill number first, since it requires no map tool).

quote: Let me get a better view of it. It's not automatically pinning the home. Are you in a single family home or a manufactured home?
stewart_read: Rep tries to keep the address-verification flowing by asking a structured qualifying question (home type) even while the mapping tool struggles — a reasonable attempt to make dead time productive.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep is just stalling for time while the map loads rather than deliberately multitasking.
coaching_implication: This specific move (asking a verify question while a tool loads) is a good habit — reinforce it, but note the rep didn't continue this pattern into bill/utility/roof questions once the map problem persisted.

quote: I'm not sure if you can zoom in or whatever, but it should be kind of like a blue with a metal on roof.
stewart_read: By this point the customer is doing most of the navigational work for the rep, describing colors and landmarks unprompted — a sign the visual-matching approach has become the customer's problem to solve, not the rep's.
coaching_implication: This is the moment the rep should have said 'no worries, let's not worry about pinning it exactly right now — I have your street address, that's enough to move forward' and pivoted back to qualifying questions.

quote: I might not have updated imagery. Let me check with my design team. This should have, like, a more updated image, and then I can just use what you described to figure it out. So let me just talk to them, and then I can give you a callback here a little bit later.
stewart_read: The call ends with a vague callback promise — no day, no time, no hour-block, no 'is that fair' handshake. None of button_up's required elements are present. The rep also abandons the entire verify section (roof age, utility company, bill amount, co-owner, tax credit) rather than completing what doesn't require the map tool.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: rep may be intentionally deferring only the address-pinning issue while planning to complete qualification on the promised callback. Rejected because the rep says goodbye and ends the call ('You have a good day. Bye bye.') rather than continuing with any remaining verify items on this same call — nothing suggests a deliberate sequencing choice.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to never let a tooling problem end the call. The address pin can be resolved by the design team asynchronously; the rep should have said 'let's keep going and I'll sort the map out on my end' and finished bill amount, utility company, and a real appointment day/time before hanging up.

quote:
It's a single family,
trailer home.
stewart_read: Customer describes the home as a 'single family, trailer home' — a manufactured/mobile home, which per Ion's general solar-installation constraints can be a non-standard scenario requiring different handling. The rep does not acknowledge or flag this distinction; the conversation dwells on visual identification instead of confirming home-type implications for eligibility.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep may not have registered the 'trailer home' phrase because it was compound with 'single family' and address-hunting was the immediate priority. Reasonable to conclude the rep simply missed it rather than deliberately deferred it.
coaching_implication: Flag for the manager: mobile/manufactured home construction can affect solar eligibility and design; the rep should confirm this detail explicitly rather than letting it pass unaddressed inside an unrelated exchange about roof color.
